data.text/markdown:
The same inference, draggable

The block above reads p(disease, given=…) off for a few fixed evidence scenarios. Here is the same disease/test model, built with core model(). clinic.show() is the whole UI: click edit on any node and drag its bars to assert a belief on that variable — every other node repaints in place, parents included (that's Dice.believe() under the hood; reset is Dice.forget()). Drag a test toward "positive" and the disease posterior climbs; pin all three fully positive and you reproduce the "3 observed positives" number above. Several dragged beliefs are satisfied jointly, so the order you drag them in doesn't matter.

Looking inside: the factor graph

The model above is a Bayes net, and its joint factorizes as ||(P(\text{disease}) \cdot \prod_i P(\text{test}_i \mid \text{disease})||). The squares below are exactly those factors — the prior and one CPT heatmap per test — drawn between the variables they connect. A pinned belief is just one more (unary) factor plugged into its variable: drag a node in the graph above (or here — these charts are live too) and watch its belief factor switch on; reset and it vanishes.

...and the joint, atom by atom

Under the hood nothing but this table exists: ||(2 \cdot 2^3 = 16||) atoms, one per full assignment, weighted by the product of the factors above. Grey bars are the prior joint; blue bars are the joint under the current beliefs. Conditioning is literally reweighting this table: pin a test positive above and watch the − atoms die and the sick atoms grow (square-root scale, because the healthy-all-negative atom dominates).
